question: Deutsche Telekom AG parent company owner
markdown:
Deutsche Telekom AG is a publicly traded company headquartered in Bonn, Germany, with no single parent company. The German government holds about 27.85% of shares directly and through KfW, while the rest is publicly traded. It is the parent of the Deutsche Telekom Group, including T-Mobile US and Telekom Deutschland, and is Europe's largest telecom company.
Deutsche Telekom AG is a publicly traded company with no single parent company or private owner.
The Federal Republic of Germany is its largest single shareholder.
The Federal Republic of Germany directly holds roughly 14.5% of the shares and another 14.5% through KfW, totaling around 27.85% state ownership.
The remaining majority of roughly 72% is publicly traded on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange and held by institutional and retail investors globally.
Deutsche Telekom operates as the ultimate parent company of the Deutsche Telekom Group.
Major subsidiaries include T-Mobile US and Telekom Deutschland.
Deutsche Telekom AG is headquartered in Bonn, Germany.
Deutsche Telekom was privatized in 1996.
Deutsche Telekom is Europe's largest telecommunications company and the world's 3rd largest.
